Each entry lists the pharmacological class, common brand names sold in India, allergen groups (used for cross-reactivity checks), and known pairwise interactions. Strengths are intentionally omitted from keys; normalisation strips them at runtime.

_cross_reactivity._comment: Groups where allergy to one member implies risk with any member of the same group. List each pair once.

penicillin_to_cephalosporin.reason: ~1-2% cross-reactivity between penicillins and cephalosporins; use cephalosporins with caution in penicillin-allergic patients

sulfa_to_sulfonylurea.reason: Structural similarity — sulfonamide-allergic patients may react to sulfonylurea oral hypoglycaemics

sulfa_to_furosemide.reason: Furosemide contains a sulfonamide moiety — risk in sulfa-allergic patients

nsaid_cross.reason: Cross-reactivity among NSAIDs is common, especially aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease
